pr_title: feat(schema,nuxt): add `shared` folder to alias and auto-imports
pr_body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

<!-- Please ensure there is an open issue and mention its number. For example, "resolves #123" -->
fix #28675

### 📚 Description

<!-- Describe your changes in detail. Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
Hello 👋,

This PR adds:

- `#shared` alias to both `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.server.json`
- Enable auto imports from `#shared/types` and `#shared/utils` in `app` and `server` directories

~_The second bullet point is still in progress because I'm still trying to understand the usage of unimport within the project._~

So, after talking with @danielroe, this `#shared` folder is more complicated than expected. Here a list of expected behavior (that needs to be implemented)

- [ ] `./app` folder can import (and auto-import) from the `./shared` folder
- [ ] `./server` folder can import (and auto-import) from the `./shared` folder
- [ ] Inside the `./shared` folder, you **should not** be able to import stuff from both `./app` and `./server` (could be achieved by excluding the file from the `tsconfig.json` and a single chunk could be created)
- [ ] Inside the`./shared` folder, you could (we need to decide if we want or not this behavior) import and auto-import stuff from the `./shared` folder.

At the end, the shared folder is just for pure JS (or TS) stuff. Nothing have to be related to Vue or Nitro.

Why not share the `utils` on default with the server?

**Something like**
```
[app]/utils/capitalize.ts // Shared with the server on default
[app]/utils/capitalize.client.ts // Client only
[app]/utils/capitalize.server.ts // Server only
```

**Advantages**
* All `utils` in a single folder
* Same ux that is already used for `components`, `pages` and `plugins`
* No need to introduce  a new `shared` folder

we now have an `app/` folder for vue server+client, and the `.server` and `.client` suffix only applies to server vs client on the vue side of the app, not to the nitro or `server/` folder, which would make using that convention somewhat confusing.

issue_context.title: Add `#shared` alias
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature

With the new directory structure, it makes sense to have a `shared/` directory for sharing constants, types and other utils between the `app/` and server/` directory.

After discussing with the core team, it makes sense to create a `#shared` alias.

```ts
// before
import { formatNumber } from '~~/shared/utils/dates'
// after
import { formatNumber } from '#shared/utils/dates'
```

It would be nice to support auto-import for `#shared/types` and `#shared/utils` as well ✨ 

### Additional information

- [ ] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

- [X] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution).
- [X] Check existing [discussions](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions) and [issues](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues).

review_comments:
sorry I know its been merged, but I was just reviewing the changes.

I was wondering, do these alias resolution keys need to be static, especially in this case, where, say, I configure the shared dir to be `common`, so my imports would still be `#shared` (that's fine, I suppose I don't make the rules! but maybe its a little friction in that dev experience), or would we rather make it align to the dir name:

```suggestion
        [`#${sanitisedSharedDirName}`]: resolve(rootDir, sharedDir),
```
I'd say that it is better to keep them static for consistency. You can always define a custom alias if you want.
